objective: Explicit staleness for time-sensitive Cash card facts, so old buying evidence becomes an unanswered task instead of silently staying current. (1) server/services/cash/staleness.ts exports a reviewed constant STALENESS_POLICY: Record<CardFieldKey | EngineFieldKey, { maxAgeDays: number } | null> — buyingEvidence (read from signal_observed_at) 30 days, revenueRange/directCosts/price from the source_date of the claim behind the card fact 90 days, everything immutable (payer identity, eligibility rule text) null — and a pure staleFields(opportunity, facts, now) that names each stale field with its observed date. `now` is always injected; nothing in the module reads the clock. (2) evidenceCard and cashEngineCard take an optional `now`; a stale field reads value null with a task beginning 'Refresh:' and the original value kept in a `staleValue` property, so the tier, markReady and the gaps pass all see it as unanswered through the one reader they already use. (3) applyOne in server/services/cash/answers.ts refuses a claim whose own source_date is already past the policy window, so research that only finds the old page does not re-close the need and loop; the need stays open and assessResearch reports it as NO_SUPPORT with that reason. (4) operate() passes its `now` to every card read. (5) Rebase every test fixture date that would cross a window as real time passes (signal_observed_at, source_date, signalObservedAt in tests/**) to dates computed relative to the test's own clock, so the suite carries no time bomb; add tests/cashStaleness.test.ts proving: a 40-day-old signal drops a READY_TO_TEST piece to QUALIFIED and raises exactly one refresh need; a fresh dated claim answers it and the tier returns; a stale claim does not; an immutable field never goes stale; a READY piece is not moved out of READY by the derivation (state is untouched, only the tier reading changes).
expectedOutcome: Old market facts reappear as research tasks automatically; nothing stale reads as current; no test depends on the wall clock.
nonGoals: A second opportunity pipeline, queue, scheduler or polling loop beside the durable Russell tick and operate()
Changing the evidence gate, verification, audit roles or approval envelopes
A full-table read on every tick; every new read is narrow, indexed and bounded

acceptanceConditions.statement: tests/cashStaleness.test.ts passes on SQLite and Postgres

rollbackRequirement: Revert the commits; any migration only adds columns with defaults or a nullable column.
